newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JULY 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JULY 30.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

-- Retail prices will be monitored more closely in an effort to pin down inflation, top government officials decided on Tuesday. The development ministry will run more frequent checks on the cost of tourist services and fuel prices. It will also ask trades unions to tone down their demands for rates increases.

-- The Bank of Greece has allowed Greek residents and legal entities to hold deposit accounts in foreign currency from August 1 and freely carry out cross-border transactions in any currency. The move rounds up the integration of the Greek economy to international markets.
-- The British pound was fixed at the Bank of Greece's fixing on Tuesday eight drachmas below its Monday level, in line with international trends.

-- Tuesday's auction of seven-year floating rate notes was succesful with the finance ministry receiving bids totalling 278 billion drachmas against its 125 billion drachma target. Bids were accepted at an average price of 90.030425 with the cut-off price at 98.84.

-- The government will cut taxation on petrol in October or November as part of its anti-inflationart strategy. It will also slash or totally remove third-party taxation currently imposed on a wide range of products and services.
-- An increasing number of Cypriot companies, including banks, trading and commercial firms, have initiated the procedure for their listing on the Athens stock exchange.

-- Following a sharp rise in blue chip prices for a few sessions, profits were taken on Tuesday driving the Athens bourse's benchmark index 1.94 percent lower. The auction of government paper that drained liquidity also contributed to the fall which was not unexpected.

-- The finance ministry is expected shortly to send yet another ultimatum to around 1,000 persons and legal entities which are grossly in arrears with their fiscal payments to settle their accounts with the tax authorities. The ministry may be forced to deprive those persons of their right to travel abroad.

-- The Public Power Corporation (PPC) will go ahead with a 3.5 percent rise in its rates effective August 1. The rates increase will not apply to large industrial clients, mostly from the metallurgical sector, who have previously struck special pricing agreements with the PPC. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
